what_it_does: checks workstream ids, parent links, cycles, required roles and people-team membership, and returns a list of error strings; all work is in memory over its two arguments.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `gc_members`, `tc_members` and `spec_sponsors` are built from `people_data` only, yet the loop at line 116 rebuilds them for every workstream. Hoisting the three sets above that loop builds each once per call. The one behaviour that moves is an exception on empty `workstreams` with `people_data` None, because `.get` then runs before the loop; the input checks decide whether that edge is tested.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `parent_kind` at line 103 is assigned and never read. The parent id was already confirmed to exist at lines 98 to 101, so the lookup cannot raise. Deleting the line removes one dict lookup and one `.get` per child workstream and changes no output.

what_it_does: scans the cached issue events for one repo and returns, for each user in `remaining`, the first event of the requested types.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The loop visits every cached event even after each user in `remaining` is already in `found`. Once `len(found) == len(remaining)` no later event can add an entry, so a break at that point returns the same dict. Both callers (lines 504 and 659) pass a set for `remaining`, which keeps the length test exact.

what_it_does: pages through the repo's issue comments since the cutoff and builds a per-user dict of PR and issue numbers, cached per repo.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `number not in commenters[user][kind]` scans a list once per comment. A set of `(user, kind, number)` kept beside the lists answers the same question with one hash probe. The lists stay as they are, so the returned dict and the order of numbers that `_check_comments` and the debug output read are unchanged.

what_it_does: inserts or re-sorts one member line in the emeritus section of a README string, creating the section if it is missing, and returns the new string.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The member-line predicate `re.match(r'^[-*+] \[', l)` runs on every section line twice: in the comprehension at 859 and in the index loop at 872. One pass that records the matching indices gives the member lines and the first and last member positions, so each line is matched once. The predicate is pure, and the output string is unchanged.

what_it_does: fetches the reviews of each candidate PR over REST and returns the first PR on which `user` has a review submitted on or after the cutoff, or None.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `_check_reviews` and `_check_reviews_paginated` call this once per user, so a PR that is a candidate for several users has its `pulls/{n}/reviews` fetched once per user. A cache of fetched reviews per `(repo, pr)`, kept as a function attribute because a repair cannot add a module-level name, removes the repeated GETs. Within one run reviews do not change, so the returned PR is the same.

what_it_does: pages through one user's GraphQL review search, verifying each candidate over REST, until it confirms a review or runs out of pages.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Batching the remaining pages across users would change which users `_check_reviews` queries and when, so the edit reaches the caller at line 409. No edit confined to this unit removes the per-user searches, so the repair cannot be written as one unit's change.

what_it_does: pages through every issue event on the repo since the cutoff and caches an (actor, event type, issue number) tuple per event per repo.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Only the types labeled, unlabeled, closed and merged are read, by `_check_events` at lines 504 and 659. Keeping only those types at line 293 means the other events are never turned into tuples or stored. The requests do not change, because the events endpoint has no type filter, so the same pages are fetched. The sole caller is `_check_events`, which filters by the same four types.

what_it_does: collects user, team and repo relationships, checks activity per repo, prints the inactive report, and optionally opens PRs.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `team_repos_map` is a local dict written at line 1356 and read nowhere in `main` or in any callee. Deleting both lines removes one `set(repos)` construction per team and no output changes.

what_it_does: builds the markdown table rows for one group of SIGs, one row per SIG.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: No edit confined to `render_group` removes the repeat. The second `extract_row_data(ws)` for the same SIG is at line 166, in `render_sig_details`, which `render_sigs_markdown` calls. Removing it needs a memo on `extract_row_data`, and that memo would be keyed on a dict, which cannot be hashed, and would outlive the call. The work is a few microseconds per SIG across about forty SIGs, and the script runs once per `make generate`.

what_it_does: looks up one contributor's GitHub login over HTTP after a 100 ms sleep, and returns None on a non-200 response.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `requests.get` without a session opens a new TCP and TLS connection on every call, and `build_devstats_rows` makes one call per contributor. A `requests.Session` created on the first call and kept on the function reuses the connection across calls. The request, headers and return value are unchanged, and the 100 ms sleep is kept.

what_it_does: walks each configured workflow's recent runs, fetches each run's jobs, and returns the bare-metal job records with their durations and queue waits.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The GitHub API has no endpoint that returns the jobs of many runs in one response, so one jobs request per run is the shortest path to the data. The card's join does not map onto a REST listing. No edit confined to this unit removes the requests.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `parse_iso(run_started_at)` is re-parsed for each job in the loop from line 110, although `run_started_at` changes once per run. Parsing it once per run, inside a try that catches ValueError and leaves the start as None, gives the same qwait: a malformed value still yields 0.0 for every job of that run, as the original does. The start of each job is already parsed without error at line 114.

what_it_does: runs `gh api --paginate` for one endpoint and yields each JSON item of the list named by `list_key`.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each call starts a `gh` process, but that process is how the script authenticates. Replacing it with a direct HTTP client changes the credential path and the error text that `collect_jobs` prints. That is a change of design, not a repair of this function.

what_it_does: reconciles the existing voter comments with the roll: removes handles no longer on it, deletes comments left empty, and posts the new voters.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: One combined pattern would not be the same edit. `remove_handle_line` ends its pattern with `\s*`, which can run across newlines, so removing one handle's line can change what the next handle's pattern matches. The comment bodies hold a few dozen lines, and each comment is followed by a `gh` call that costs more than the regex passes.

what_it_does: turns the devstats frames into [login, contributions] rows, with one GitHub lookup per name.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `zip(names, contributions)` is not identical here. If `contributions` is shorter than `names`, the index loop raises IndexError, while zip truncates silently, and `zip(..., strict=True)` raises ValueError instead. The per-item cost is one network lookup and a 100 ms sleep, so the index arithmetic saves nothing measurable.

what_it_does: for each batch of ten users, sends one GraphQL search, verifies the candidate PRs over REST, paginates per user where needed, and returns the users with a confirmed review.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The `safe` alias `"u_" + re.sub(...)` is computed for each user when the batch query is built (line 433) and again when the result is read (line 449). Keeping the alias from line 433 in a list or dict and reading it at line 449 gives the same value without a second `re.sub` and concatenation per user. The function's output is unchanged.

what_it_does: checks whether each user is active on one repo through PR comments, issue comments, reviews, authored PRs and merges, and returns the active set.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The `safe` alias is computed for each user when the authored-PR query is built (line 631) and again when the result is read (line 646). Keeping the alias from line 631 and reading it at line 646 removes one `re.sub` and one concatenation per user. The returned set is unchanged.

what_it_does: lists the member entries in the text of a README section as dicts with name, username and matched line.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The loop over `member_re.finditer(text)` does nothing but `members.append({...})`, so each item pays a bound-method lookup and a call. The same list built as a comprehension over the same `finditer` removes both per item. The body is only the dict construction, so the output is identical.

what_it_does: for each repo with inactive members, fetches its README, moves each inactive user to the emeritus section, and opens or updates a pull request.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: `user.lower()` in the comparison at line 1211 is evaluated for every member line of each role section, and `user` does not change inside the inner loop. Computing it once before the `for m in _parse_members(...)` loop removes one call per member line. The branch taken is the same.
